modules.title: Keys & Recovery Phrases
lessons: A wallet doesn't store coins. It stores keys that prove you can spend them on the Bitcoin network.
Your private key signs transactions. Anyone who has it controls your Bitcoin. Your address is safe to share.
Your recovery phrase (12 or 24 words) can rebuild your wallet on any compatible device. Treat it like the keys themselves.
A PIN only unlocks the app on one device. It is NOT a backup and cannot recover your funds.

simulation.prompt: You lost your phone. It had your wallet app. You have a new phone. What do you do first?

choices.text: Reinstall the wallet and restore using my offline recovery phrase backup.
choices.feedback: Correct. The phrase rebuilds your wallet.

choices.text: Email support with my PIN so they can reset it.
choices.feedback: Self-custody has no support desk. A PIN can't restore a wallet.

choices.text: Check if my PIN works on the new phone.
choices.feedback: A PIN is tied to the old device. Without the phrase, access is gone.

quiz.q: What actually lets you recover a wallet on a new device?
Who should you share your recovery phrase with?
Which is safe to share to receive Bitcoin?
If your Bitcoin sits on an exchange, who holds the private keys?

modules.title: Backups & Scams
lessons: Phishing: fake sites, DMs and 'support' agents ask for your phrase. Real wallets never will.
Back up your phrase on paper or metal, offline. Not in screenshots, notes apps, email or cloud storage.
Keep backups in more than one secure place, and test recovery with a small amount first.
Hardware wallets keep keys on a dedicated device, so a hacked phone or laptop can't steal them.

simulation.prompt: A 'wallet support' DM says your wallet is at risk and asks you to verify by typing your 12 words on their link.

choices.text: Type the words quickly to secure my funds.
choices.feedback: Classic scam. Anyone with your words controls your Bitcoin.

choices.text: Ignore and report it. Support never needs my phrase.
choices.feedback: Correct. Never enter your phrase on a website or in a chat.

quiz.q: Best place for a recovery phrase backup?
A stranger offers wallet 'support' and asks for your words. You...
Why test a recovery with a small amount first?
options: To prove the backup works before trusting it with everything

quiz.q: A website says 'validate your wallet' by entering your words. This is...
How does a hardware wallet reduce risk?
options: Keys stay on a dedicated device, away from your phone or laptop
It hides your transactions from the network

sims.title: Phishing inbox
sims.intro: Six messages just landed. Decide what to do with each one.
sims.wrap: Pattern to remember: real services never ask for your words, and urgency is a warning sign.

card.subject: Urgent: verify your recovery phrase
card.body: Your wallet will be frozen in 24 hours. Reply with your 12 words to keep access.

scenes.q: Scam or safe?

options.fb: Wallets and support never ask for your words.
Anyone with your words controls your Bitcoin.

card.subject: New app version available
card.body: A new version is out. Update from your official app store. We never ask for your recovery phrase.

scenes.q: Scam or safe?

options.fb: Not everything is a scam. This asks for nothing and points to the official store.

options.t: Safe: update only through the official store
options.fb: It asks for nothing sensitive.

card.subject: Send 0.01 BTC, get 0.1 BTC back!
card.body: Limited giveaway. Send first to verify your address.

scenes.q: Scam or safe?

options.t: Send a little to try it
options.fb: Giveaways that ask you to send first are always scams.
Nobody doubles your Bitcoin.

card.subject: Your device needs validating
card.body: Enter your recovery phrase at the link below to validate your device.

scenes.q: Spot the trick in the link.

options.t: The link starts with yourwallet.com, so it's fine
options.fb: The real domain is what comes right before the first slash: verify-device.xyz.

options.t: Fake domain, and it asks for my words
options.fb: Two red flags in one message.

card.subject: Quick favour
card.body: I'm stuck abroad. Can you send me 50,000 sats on Lightning right now?

scenes.q: What do you do?

options.fb: Hijacked accounts are common.

options.t: Call them on a number I already have
options.fb: Confirm on a channel you already trust.

card.subject: Withdrawal confirmation code
card.body: You requested a withdrawal. If this wasn't you, secure your account.

scenes.q: What do you do?

options.t: Safe if I made the request. If not, secure my account on the official site
options.fb: Never use links in the message to log in.

options.t: Share the code with whoever asks
options.fb: Codes are for you only.

modules.title: Passphrases, Paths & Planning
lessons: A passphrase is an extra word added to your recovery phrase. A different passphrase opens a different wallet. Lose it and those funds are unrecoverable.
The same phrase can show different addresses if a wallet uses a different derivation path or address type. A zero balance after restoring may just mean the wrong path.
Verify receiving addresses on your hardware wallet's own screen. Malware on your computer can swap what the computer shows.
Multisig needs several keys to spend, such as 2 of 3, so losing or leaking one key doesn't sink you.
Plan for emergencies: a trusted person should know where backups are and how recovery works, without holding your funds early.

simulation.prompt: You restore the correct phrase in a new wallet app and see 0 sats. What do you check first?

choices.text: Assume the funds were stolen and panic.
choices.feedback: Premature. Check the common causes first.

choices.text: Check for a passphrase and the derivation path or address type.
choices.feedback: Correct. These are the usual reasons a restore looks empty.

choices.text: Reinstall again and again until the balance appears.
choices.feedback: Repeating the same restore changes nothing.

quiz.q: You restore the right phrase but the balance is 0. What do you check first?
options: Whether a passphrase, path or address type differs

quiz.q: You forgot your passphrase but still have your 24 words. What happens?
options: Funds behind that passphrase are unrecoverable
The wallet generates a new one for you

quiz.q: Why verify a receive address on the hardware wallet's screen?
options: Malware can alter the address shown on your computer
Losing one key doesn't lose the funds
Steel backups in separate secure places plus a tested recovery

sims.title: Hardware wallet setup
sims.intro: Your new hardware wallet just arrived. Set it up safely.
sims.wrap: Your keys are born on your own device, backed up offline, and guarded separately from any passphrase.

scenes.q: The box seal looks cut and re-glued.

options.t: Use it anyway, it's probably fine
options.fb: A tampered device can be pre-loaded to steal funds.

options.t: Don't use it. Contact the seller for a replacement
options.fb: Never trust a device with a broken seal.

scenes.q: A card with 12 words is already in the box, 'for convenience'.

options.fb: Pre-printed words mean someone else knows your keys.

options.t: Ignore the card. Generate new words on the device
options.fb: Only words made on your own device are yours.

scenes.q: The device shows your own words. What do you do?

options.t: Take a photo so I don't lose them
options.fb: Photos sync to clouds and get hacked.

options.t: Write them by hand on the backup card and keep it offline
options.fb: Offline and handwritten.

scenes.q: Confirmation: which is word #3?

options.fb: Check your card.
Correct.
Check your card.

scenes.q: Confirmation: which is word #8?

options.fb: Correct.
Check your card.
Check your card.

scenes.q: The device offers an optional passphrase. What does it do?

options.fb: The PIN and passphrase are different things.

options.t: Adds an extra word that opens a separate hidden wallet
options.fb: Different passphrase, different wallet.
It's not a backup.

scenes.q: You choose the passphrase 'northstar'. Where do you keep it?

options.t: On the same card as my words
options.fb: One thief would get both.

options.t: Written separately, stored in a different secure place
options.fb: Keep it apart from the words.
Digital copies get hacked.

scenes.q: Later you forget the passphrase. Your words are safe. What happens to the funds under it?

options.fb: There is no support desk.

options.t: They're unrecoverable, so guard it like the words
options.fb: Exactly.

options.t: The words alone still open them
options.fb: The words alone open a different, empty wallet.

sims.title: Send safely
sims.intro: You're paying a friend. Compare the address on your computer with the one on your hardware wallet.
sims.wrap: Compare every chunk on the device screen. Attackers can match the first and last characters.

scenes.q: What do you do?

options.fb: Every chunk matches.
They're identical. Compare chunk by chunk.

scenes.q: What do you do?

options.fb: One character differs. Malware swaps addresses after you copy them.
Caught it.

scenes.q: The start and end match. What now?

options.fb: Attackers match the ends on purpose.

options.t: Compare every chunk, find the difference, reject
options.fb: The middle differs.

sims.title: Multisig builder
sims.intro: You're protecting serious savings. Design a 2-of-3 setup.
sims.wrap: Multisig removes the single point of failure: no single loss or leak is fatal.

scenes.q: Which setup removes a single point of failure?

options.fb: Lose or leak it and you're done.
Any two of three keys can spend.
Losing any one key locks the funds.

scenes.q: Where do the three keys go?

options.t: All three in my home safe
options.fb: One fire or burglary takes all three.

options.t: Home safe, bank box, trusted relative
options.fb: Separate places.
Phones get hacked and lost.

scenes.q: A fire destroys the key in your home safe. Can you still spend?

options.fb: You still hold two of three keys.

options.t: Yes, with the other two keys
options.fb: Then move funds to a fresh setup.
Any two keys work.

scenes.q: A burglar steals one key. Can they spend?

options.fb: They need a second key.

options.t: No, but I should move funds to a new setup soon
options.fb: Don't wait for them to find another.
